verdict.rationale: Otter documents some admin controls—SSO/identity integration, audit trails/activity logs, and OAuth-scoped granular permissions for its MCP server—suggesting some sharing governance (otter-docs-19, otter-docs-20, otter-docs-47, otter-docs-52, otter-docs-35). However, multiple independent community reports concretely contradict the 'private-by-default' premise: users report Otter shares transcripts with all meeting participants by default without consent, and specific incidents of confidential meeting content being leaked or emailed to third parties (otter-comm-2, otter-comm-3, otter-comm-5, otter-comm-6, otter-comm-7, otter-comm-8). missing for 10: verified private-by-default note settings, documented folder/workspace-level permission granularity, and evidence the admin visibility features actually prevent the default-sharing behavior reported by users.
